source_snapshot.criteria: Command should be sent without any error.
source_snapshot.script: DQMS link names 91.BMC_Cold-Reset.sh, which is unrelated to the stated button-enable operation.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL says exact bytes are needed and flags a chassis write.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED requires vendor command schema, button bitmap, readback and restore because it does not identify the standard Chassis command or payload.

old_problem: The historical record correctly rejected the source bytes but concluded that only a vendor contract could resolve them. IPMI 2.0 defines this exact optional Chassis command: NetFn 00h/Cmd 0Ah with one mask byte, not App NetFn 06h/Cmd 0Ah with no data. It also defines the bit map and standard readback in Get Chassis Status byte 5. The cold-reset script is a mismatched artifact, not missing authority. Remaining platform-supported buttons, press procedure and service-impact recovery are Project execution inputs.
disposition_reason: Replace the wrong source raw request only in the review layer with standard in-band Chassis 00h/0Ah plus one reserved-clean mask byte. Read Get Chassis Status 00h/01h byte 5 to discover per-button disable capability and baseline state. For each supported, enabled and separately approved Power-off, Reset, Diagnostic Interrupt or Standby function, disable only that one bit while preserving the other three, require exact readback, have a qualified operator perform the physical button action and capture genuine visual/system evidence that the function is inhibited, then restore the baseline and verify both readback and approved positive behavior/recovery. Never disable multiple recovery controls together, run the cold-reset script, infer unsupported bits, clear logs, automate a physical press, retry a failed write or let the agent initiate power/reset/diagnostic/sleep actions.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1054-1056, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests_gpt_merged, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The code is unique. Related OOB row 1182 / Wistron-BMC-00472-V003 was directly read and remains a separate Source Key/Variant. Formal queue sequence 65 was independently verified as row 1056 / variant 5c055baf414bb636.

IPMI v2.0 section 28.6 and Appendix G assign Set Front Panel Button Enables to Chassis NetFn 00h, command 0Ah. The source's App NetFn 06h is authoritative-command conflict, and absence of the required request byte makes its command incapable of setting the stated controls.

Table 28-7 defines request bits 3..0 as 1=disable Standby, Diagnostic Interrupt, Reset and Power-off respectively, with bits 7..4 reserved zero. There is no OEM payload needed for the standard function.

Get Chassis Status Chassis 00h/01h optional response byte 5 returns capability bits 7..4 and present disabled-state bits 3..0 for the same four controls. A bit may be tested only when its paired capability bit is 1; an absent byte or capability 0 is authoritative unsupported evidence for per-bit N/A.

Command completion alone cannot satisfy the functional title. Exact status readback proves BMC state, while a qualified human must supply the physical button observation. This preserves ED-09 and avoids claiming remote visual/physical execution.

A disabled Power-off bit also disables sleep requests when power/sleep share one physical button, while the Standby-disable bit still permits wake. The Project button map and press-duration/action fixture must distinguish combined controls before any physical step.

Power-off, reset, diagnostic interrupt and standby positive checks can affect availability or OS integrity. Each physical action needs its own approved maintenance/recovery gate; missing approval leaves that supported subcase NOT READY, not falsely PASS or N/A.
The source's linked cold-reset script neither names nor safely implements this command and would add an unrelated reset. It is retained as history but explicitly excluded from execution and evidence.

ED-03/ED-09/ED-13 resolve standard BMC and manual physical boundaries; ED-15 limits N/A to capability evidence; ED-18/ED-19 preserve exact power/control state and logs; ED-28/ED-30 require isolated recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 govern packages, confirmation, cleanup, non-retry and engineer verdict separation.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Set Front Panel Button Enables (IB Chassis 00h/0Ah) per-button disable, manual behavior and restore
test_case.purpose: For every front-panel function the chassis says can be disabled, prove through the in-band standard command, exact status readback and qualified manual observation that one button at a time is inhibited, then restore its original state and confirm the physical control and platform recover correctly without conflating the separate OOB variant.
required_package: Approved SUT/chassis/BMC/firmware and local IPMI system interface, plus independent OOB console and a qualified physical operator at the exact chassis

Get Chassis Status App 00h/01h baseline including optional byte 5, decoded capability nibble and disabled-state nibble; physical front-panel map identifying separate or combined power/standby, reset and diagnostic controls

Owner-approved per-button matrix for every supported function: bit, baseline state, press type/duration, expected disabled behavior, expected restored behavior, service impact, OS/data-safety preparation and recovery

Validated ipmitool/raw runner using in-band `-I open` Chassis 00h/0Ah with exactly one mask byte, reserved-bit validation, 00h/01h readback parser, exact baseline restore, explicit zero automatic retries and package version/hash

Timestamped manual evidence mechanism (video/photo plus operator checklist and console/log correlation), stable management observation, preserved SEL/system logs and immediate confirmation before each state-changing command and each physical press
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED MIXED AUTOMATION/MANUAL PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve SEL/system/audit logs; do not clear them and do not run the linked cold-reset script. Over the local system interface read Chassis 00h/01h, require optional byte 5, decode CAP=bits7:4 and BASE_DISABLED=bits3:0, validate the physical button map and approved per-button matrix. For each supported capability bit whose baseline state and physical action are approved, process exactly one button before the next: compute TEST_MASK=BASE_DISABLED OR TARGET_BIT with bits7:4 zero; display button, mask, recovery and service impact for immediate approval; send exactly once in-band Chassis 00h/0Ah [TEST_MASK], require completion 00h and read 00h/01h byte5 until one deterministic read shows only TARGET_BIT disabled. A qualified human—not the agent—performs only the approved button action while video, OOB console, power/OS state and logs record that the corresponding function is inhibited. Send exactly once 00h/0Ah [BASE_DISABLED], require 00h and exact byte5 baseline. The operator then supplies the separately approved positive-behavior evidence and recovery for that button; confirm stable expected platform state and logs before proceeding. Unsupported bits are N/A from capability only; already-disabled policy bits require an owner-approved enable/restore plan or remain NOT READY. Never send source 06h/0Ah, omit the mask, disable more than one new bit, automate a press, trigger power/reset/NMI/sleep, retry, clear logs or continue after failed restoration.
test_case.expected_result: The source conflict is corrected to Chassis 00h/0Ah with one reserved-clean mask. For each supported approved button, the single disable returns 00h; Get Chassis Status byte 5 preserves capabilities and all non-target states while the target disabled bit becomes 1. Qualified operator evidence shows the intended physical function is inhibited and no other button behavior changes. The single restore returns 00h and byte 5 matches the exact baseline; approved manual positive evidence and recovery confirm the restored control. OOB access, OS/data integrity, logs and unrelated chassis state remain healthy. Missing optional byte/capability yields per-bit N/A; command/readback/behavior mismatch, unintended action, timeout or failed restore is FAIL/NOT READY without retry.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact Source Key/variant, correct 00h/0Ah identity and one-byte mask, capability-backed scope, one-bit-at-a-time changes, 00h completions, byte-5 state equality, genuine operator physical evidence for disabled and restored behavior, exact baseline restore and no collateral power/reset/NMI/sleep/log effect. Source 06h/0Ah, no payload, cold-reset script, command success alone, readback without physical evidence, unsupported-bit inference, multiple disabled recovery controls, agent-generated/claimed press evidence, unapproved service action, retry, log clearing or incomplete restore cannot pass. Supported but unapproved physical action is NOT READY; N/A requires byte-5 capability evidence.
safety_gate: Use only the local in-band system interface for this IB identity and keep independent OOB observation/recovery live. The separate row 1182 OOB variant cannot be credited here.
Read and decode capability/status before writing. Reserved high mask bits are zero; preserve all baseline disabled bits and introduce at most one additional disable bit per subtest.

A qualified human performs all button presses. The agent must not press or remotely emulate Power, Reset, Diagnostic Interrupt or Standby and must not claim visual/physical evidence it did not receive.

Each physical action has a dedicated maintenance gate: quiesced data, expected system transition, OOB console and recovery. Never combine power and reset lockout or remove the sole physical recovery path.
Preserve SEL, system and audit evidence. Do not run the unrelated cold-reset script, power cycle, reset, inject NMI, enter sleep or clear logs as automated recovery.

No automatic retry. On timeout or ambiguous state, stop physical action, read status through the independent path, restore BASE_DISABLED once if needed and hand remaining recovery to the chassis owner.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; SUT/chassis/BMC/firmware/system-interface identity; correct standard-command authority; separate row-1182 OOB identity retained
Raw/decoded baseline Get Chassis Status byte 5, capability-to-status mapping, physical button/combined-control map and per-button approval matrix
Runner/version/hash and per-button redacted 00h/0Ah request mask, completion and byte-5 readback proving only the intended disabled bit changed
Timestamped operator video/photo/checklist with OOB console, power/OS state and log correlation showing disabled behavior for each supported approved physical control
Per-button baseline restore request/readback and separately approved restored positive-behavior/recovery evidence
Unchanged unrelated controls, access, data/log health; per-bit PASS/FAIL/NOT READY/N/A table and engineer verdict without DUT execution claims by the review agent
test_case.recovery: Before every subtest precompute Chassis 00h/0Ah [BASE_DISABLED]. If the disable response is ambiguous, prohibit the physical press, read Get Chassis Status through local/OOB observation and send the exact baseline mask once only if state differs. If a physical action unexpectedly powers off, resets, interrupts or sleeps the host, stop the matrix, preserve video/console/SEL/system evidence and let the authorized operator follow that button's documented recovery; the agent must not power cycle or retry. Verify byte 5, OS/data health, OOB access and all unrelated controls before closure.

source_conflict.reason: Official section 28.6 resolves the title-command conflict: the review layer corrects App 06h/no-data to Chassis 00h/0Ah with one mask byte, rejects the cold-reset script and replaces success-only criteria with standard readback, manual behavior and restore without editing Master history.

blocked.reason: Core command, bit map, readback and unsupported criteria are standardized. Chassis capability, physical map, per-button service authorization, operator evidence and recovery are finite Project execution prerequisites.

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7
external_authorities.application: Section 28.6/Table 28-7 and Appendix G define Chassis 00h/Cmd 0Ah, the required one-byte Standby/Diagnostic/Reset/Power disable mask and reserved bits; section 28.2 Get Chassis Status byte 5 defines capability and present-disable readback.

project_authority: The Project chassis/BMC owners provide the capability/button map, approve every physical action and service-recovery sequence, validate the in-band runner and issue per-bit and overall verdicts. They may mark a function N/A only from authoritative capability/SPEC evidence. Approval cannot use the wrong source bytes or cold-reset script, automate physical presses, disable multiple recovery controls, omit real physical evidence, retry automatically, clear logs or accept incomplete restore.
